line: resumed core research prototype, real tasks (coding)

SEAM.note: one reverse_words 'verify+retry' was most likely a transient API timeout (graceful ''->retry), not a genuine model error

NO_VERIFY.note: model got everything right -> no errors for verification to catch

honest_reading: The seam runs end-to-end on real coding with a real model (proposer=Kimi; causal world model=interventional verification by running tests; governable disposer=confidence-gated escalation; metric=interventions/task). On this task set the strong model solves 11/11 first-try, including the hard edge-case tasks (atoi clamp, IPv4 leading-zeros, integer-division eval) -> 0 interventions, 0 silent failures, BUT also 0 silent failures for NO-VERIFY, so the arms do not differentiate. The task set is within the model's competence; the experiment validates the architecture but does NOT yet demonstrate the seam's value.
product_insight: The seam's value is FRONTIER-DEPENDENT. It is NOT what makes the model capable (it already is, on these tasks) -- it is what makes the model TRUSTWORTHY TO RUN UNATTENDED: verification catches its failures and escalation surfaces its uncertainty, instead of silently committing garbage. On tasks the model nails, the seam is invisible (0 interventions either way); on tasks at/beyond the model's edge it is exactly what lets you deploy it autonomously. To MEASURE the value, push to the model's failure frontier (genuinely hard / ambiguous / multi-step real tasks where strong models fail) -- there, SEAM (catch+escalate, 0 silent failures, interventions << always-ask) visibly differentiates from NO-VERIFY (silent broken commits) and ALWAYS-ASK (max interventions).
